data.title: Find out what agents init and job init do to an existing project
data.description:
The setup has to be safe in a project that already has files, and `SETUP.md` should be written from what these tools actually do. The `agents init` help says existing `AGENTS.md` content becomes the project-owned head and that it links `CLAUDE.md`. No one has yet checked a real `CLAUDE.md` file with no `AGENTS.md`, or a symlink, an existing `.gitignore`, a folder that isn't a Git repo, or a second run.

Try each case in a scratch folder, with `AGENTS_REGISTRY` and `AGENTS_CACHE` pointed at scratch so Ben's real registry stays clean. Fix a tool bug at its source, or file it, rather than working around it in the playbook.

data.title: Ship the Go tools as signed bottles
data.description:
`job` and `agents` only install with `go install`, and `contextfill` builds from source, so a new user would need Go. Add formulae for `job` and `agents` to `homebrew-tap`, and set `bottle=yes`, `sign=` and `notary_profile=` in each tool's `scripts/release.conf`, following `woodcase`'s. Each tool releases itself with `homebrew-tap`'s `scripts/release`.

Check each repo is public first; `gh` was blocked in the sandbox when this plan was written. Releases push tags and upload bottles, so they need Ben's OK and his signing credentials. Update each README's install section to lead with `brew install bensyverson/tap/<tool>`.

Risk: bottles are tagged for the formula's oldest macOS, and the binary must target that release.

criteria.label: brew install of job, agents and contextfill pours a bottle with no Go installed, shown on a clean account
codesign and spctl checks pass on each binary

data.title: Ship sleepy and peep as signed bottles
data.description:
Neither tool is in the tap: `sleepy` (repo `sleepyhollow`) and `peep` (repo `PixelPeeper`) install from source today. Add formulae and bottles the same way `woodcase` does, including any resource bundle that has to sit beside the binary.

Two traps. `sleepy`'s `Package.swift` deliberately pins the macOS 12 SDK at link time because WebKit gates behavior on it, so a build that loses that flag can pass and still behave wrongly. `PixelPeeper` has no LICENSE file, and Ben needs to confirm one before it ships publicly.

Same release constraints as the Go tools: Ben's OK and his signing credentials.

criteria.label: brew install of sleepy and peep pours a bottle without Xcode, shown on a clean account
otool -l on the bottled sleepy shows the same SDK version as a source build
PixelPeeper has a LICENSE

data.title: Write the README, SETUP.md and Brewfile
data.description:
This is the product. The plan doc's "How the link works" and "Setup order" sections hold the agreed flow, including the Homebrew, `gh` and `PATH` steps, and its "Decisions" section binds this leaf.

Write for someone who may never have used a terminal: explain each tool in a sentence or two. Keep the README tight and put the steps in `SETUP.md`. `SETUP.md` also creates `local/` and explains it, because that rule lives here. Installing the tools depends on the bottle leaves for real use, but the text can be written before they ship.

data.old_desc:

data.new_desc:
This is what a new user sees and reads. It turns the approved prototype into a real signed program, so an agent can show progress and collect choices on a Mac that may have nothing installed.

**What exists when it's done:** a Go program, `bootstrap`, with a library core and a thin CLI. It serves the page on 127.0.0.1 and gives the agent a small JSON command line along the lines of detect, serve, step and wait. The agent still does the installing. All screens and copy live in the binary, so an agent can't invent wording, and the launching agent's name comes from a flag.

**Already decided (Ben, 2026-11-05):** Go, signed and notarized. Threads, in linear light. No hard cuts: every change animates, and what leaves and what arrives share one 1.4s S-curve. The object never moves. See "The interface" in project/2026-11-05-setup-link-plan.md. The prototype in project/2026-11-05-setup-page-mock/prototype/ is the visual reference, including its timing constants and shaders. Its bottom study bar, fake waits and "I did it" buttons are not part of the product.

**Seams:** new Go module in this repo. Embed the page, Three.js (no CDN), the subset Grand fonts and the card images. One shared struct for events across the CLI and the page.

**Security:** bind to loopback, require a random token, check Host and Origin, exit after the agent stops sending heartbeats. Test each refusal.

**Open:** real data for the Homebrew and Git cards, which are made up in the prototype. Long steps may only be able to show elapsed time. The agent's call on the exact verbs.

**Risks:** the float buffer costs more to draw on weak Macs, so keep an eight-bit path. An agent may hesitate to run a downloaded binary, tested in its own leaf.

Does xcode-select --install, then Homebrew, then the tools work from nothing in a clean VM? Can the file /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/git be polled to detect the end of Apple's install? Do the threads run smoothly on the MacBook Air?

**If an agent refuses the binary:** consider a script bootstrap, a clearer SETUP.md, or starting in chat. Record which.

data.title: Build the bootstrap core
data.description:
The `bootstrap` binary needs a library that holds its decisions, with the CLI and server as thin layers over it. This leaf makes that library. Everything else in the binary builds on it.

What exists when it's done: a Go module at the repo root using only the standard library, with cgo off. `bootstrap`, `detect`, `tools` and `screens` work, printing terse rows by default and a stable shape with `--json`, and none of them needs a session. The catalog of tools lives in `catalog/tools.json`, embedded in the binary and readable as a raw file, so the chat fallback in `SETUP.md` can use the same facts when the binary can't run. The screens from the prototype are defined in Go as closed lists, each producing the description the page draws, including the swap of `{app}` and `{ai}` for Claude Code or OpenCode. Progress is calculated from the screen, the tool and the user's choices; callers never pass a percentage.

Already decided (project/2026-11-05-setup-link-plan.md, "The interface", and project/2026-11-05-bootstrap-binary-plan.md): Go; all copy in the binary; very few words at a 6th-grade reading level; the tool is called Jobs in anything a person reads. Detect Apple's tools by `/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/git`, never `xcode-select -p` or `command -v git`, because `/usr/bin/git` is a stub until they're installed. Copy each screen's words from the `SCREENS` object in project/2026-11-05-setup-page-mock/prototype/template.html.

Seams: the leaf "Build the server and CLI" consumes this; the leaf "Port the page" draws the description. Check in one JSON sample per screen, generated and compared by a Go test, because JavaScript can't import a Go struct and the page is the other side of that seam.

Out of scope: the server, the page and signing. The "needs a newer Mac" screen is dropped, since an arm64 binary can't start on an Intel Mac. The prototype's study bar and fake waits aren't part of the product.

The house CLI rules bind this leaf and the server leaf: read project/agents/cli-design.md. They cover the primer, one shape per verb, the shared exit codes, errors that name the next command, and tests that drive the binary.

The agent's call: exact field names and package layout, keeping files small.

criteria.label: A table test shows detect reports each missing and present state, using a fake filesystem root, including Apple's tools absent while /usr/bin/git exists
A test driving the binary shows an unknown screen, tool or status exits 2 and lists the valid values
A test shows a bare bootstrap prints the primer with no session and no network
A test shows every screen's description matches its checked-in JSON sample, for both Claude Code and OpenCode
A test shows progress never goes down across the screen order, with tools skipped
catalog/tools.json loads from the embedded copy, and a test shows every tool on the list screen is in it

data.title: Build the server and CLI
data.description:
This is how the agent and the page talk. An agent runs short commands and a person clicks in a browser, and this leaf connects the two without opening anything to the rest of the machine.

What exists when it's done: `bootstrap serve --agent <name>` detaches itself, binds to 127.0.0.1 on a free port, opens the browser with `/usr/bin/open`, and reports the URL and whether the browser opened. The session is an append-only JSONL log readable only by its owner. `show` appends to it, the page's answers land in it, `wait` and `status` read it, and `stop` ends the session. The commands never talk to the server. The server tails the log, sends new screens to the page over Server-Sent Events, and appends the answers it receives. `wait answer|clt|brew` returns what it waited for, or exits 3 with "still waiting, run wait again". Answers to an earlier screen are never returned.

Already decided (project/2026-11-05-setup-link-plan.md): bind to loopback, require a random token on the page's requests, check Host and Origin, exit after the agent is gone. Standard library only. From project/2026-11-05-bootstrap-binary-plan.md: every command renews a time allowance, three minutes by default or longer with `show --expect`. Past it while the agent is working, the page shows the lost screen, "Whoops! We lost your {app} session. Open it back up and type “continue”." (Ben's wording). While the page waits on the user nothing changes until they click, when the click is saved and the lost screen appears if no agent has checked recently. The next command from any session brings the page back. The server keeps running while the tab is open, up to about an hour, then exits, and `serve` starts fresh from the same log. A second `serve` reuses a live session. A typed project name must be a safe folder name, because an agent will use it in commands. The house CLI rules bind this leaf: project/agents/cli-design.md.

Seams: the library from "Build the bootstrap core" holds the decisions; this layer stays thin. The page is another leaf, so test with plain HTTP clients.

Open, the agent's call: where bootstrap's folder lives, which pro mode's preferences file (t5FAqu) will share. Open for the trial, so make them easy to change: the default `wait` timeout, and the exact lost-screen line.

Risks: `serve` must fail with clear JSON rather than hang when it can't bind or open a browser, because that failure is what sends the agent to the chat fallback. A sandboxed agent can't bind a port or run `open`, and that should read as a normal fallback. A machine sleeping through an allowance shouldn't count as the agent leaving, or at least should recover when it wakes.

criteria.label: Tests show a request is refused for each of a missing token, a wrong token, a wrong Host and a wrong Origin
A test shows the server binds only to the loopback address
Tests show the lost screen appears past the allowance while working, and only after a click while waiting on the user
A test shows the next command after a lost screen brings the page back
A test shows a click with no agent is saved and a later status reports it
A test shows the server exits once the tab is closed or the hour is up
Tests driving the binary show wait returns an answer and a clt or brew arrival at exit 0, and exit 3 with the remedy when time runs out
A test shows wait answer never returns an answer to an earlier screen
A test shows serve exits 5 with a remedy when it can't bind, and doesn't hang
A test shows the log is readable only by its owner, and that an unsafe project name is refused
A live run of serve, show, wait and stop leaves no process behind, shown by pgrep on the printed pid

data.title: Port the page from the prototype
data.description:
This is what a new user actually sees, and Ben has approved its look and motion. The job is to carry that across faithfully while removing everything that only served the study.

What exists when it's done: a page embedded in the binary that draws any screen from the description the server sends. It holds the threads, the transitions, the fonts and the cards, and knows nothing about any particular screen's wording. A preview route draws every screen in each state from the checked-in JSON samples, for review and for still tests.

Already decided (Ben, 2026-11-05; project/2026-11-05-setup-link-plan.md, "The interface"): silk threads in linear light, blue through cyan to green with progress, relaxing to the starting form. No hard cuts: what leaves and what arrives share one 1.4s S-curve, and the object never moves. Fast while working, slow while waiting. Grand Medium for titles and Regular for buttons, subset to Latin. Three.js r128, the fonts and the images are embedded, with no CDN. Copy the shaders and timing constants from project/2026-11-05-setup-page-mock/prototype/template.html rather than rewriting them.

Keep the prototype's reduced-motion handling, and its eight-bit path for when the float buffer isn't available. Keep Three.js's license with the vendored copy. Tool names link to their repos.

Out of scope: the bottom study bar, fake waits and "I did it" buttons. Real card contents for Homebrew, Git and Woodcase belong to the full-screens leaf.

Risks: headless Sleepy never ticks animation frames, so a page that fades in screenshots as blank. Test stills through the preview route at rest. Live motion can only be judged in a real browser, so Ben reviews it. The server sends no third-party requests, so a Content-Security-Policy can prove the page loads nothing from outside.

criteria.label: Sleepy stills of every screen through the preview route, compared against the prototype with peep, show no unexplained differences
The page loads with the network off and a strict Content-Security-Policy, with no console errors, shown by sleepy
No overflow at 400px wide on any screen, shown by sleepy
The page shows the lost screen when the server goes away, with no request needed, shown by a live run
Ben has reviewed the live motion in a real browser and approved it, recorded in a note

data.title: Publish a signed trial release
data.description:
The agent trial (Y6LsGy) asks whether an agent, given only a pasted link, will verify and run a signed binary. That needs a real signed file at a public URL. It could change the design, so it comes before the rest of the screens.

What exists when it's done: `scripts/release` in this repo builds for darwin/arm64 with cgo off, signs with the Developer ID identity (the same one as project woodcase's scripts/release.conf), notarizes, and uploads a bare file with its checksum to a GitHub release of the public bensyverson/bootstrap. A thin README and a stub SETUP.md say enough for the trial: what this is, what will change, how to fetch, verify and start it. The welcome and list screens work end to end.

Already decided: public repo bensyverson/bootstrap, approved by Ben. Fetched with curl since Homebrew may not exist yet; SETUP.md pins a version and checksum and the agent verifies those and the signature before running it (project/2026-11-05-setup-link-plan.md).

Needs Ben: his OK on timing, and his signing and notary credentials, which a sandboxed agent can't reach. Pushing a release is outward-facing, so ask at the moment of doing it.

Open, to settle here: the tap's `scripts/release` publishes formulae and bottles rather than a bare file, so this needs its own small script, and Ben has yet to rule on when it goes public. Confirm which notary profile applies. Confirm that `codesign` and `spctl` run with no developer tools, and whether a bare binary can be stapled; as far as we know it can't, so `spctl` may need a network check. Set the oldest macOS the binary targets and state it.

Out of scope: the full README and SETUP.md (W2yASt), and the tap formula, which can come later.

criteria.label: A file fetched with curl from the public release passes the checksum, codesign and spctl checks the stub SETUP.md lists, shown by a recorded run
The release URL and raw SETUP.md load with no sign-in, shown by curl with no credentials
Ben has approved the timing, recorded in a note
A request without the token is refused by the released binary, shown by curl

data.title: Finish every screen and the real cards
data.description:
The trial release only needs two screens. This leaf finishes the rest, after the trial has shown whether the design holds, so it isn't built on a premise that's about to move.

What exists when it's done: every prototype screen works through `show`, in Claude Code's and OpenCode's names: Apple's tools, Homebrew, each tool, the project questions, GitHub, the phone, done, trouble and lost. Cards show real captures instead of the invented ones. The Homebrew, Git, Contextfill and Woodcase cards in the prototype are made up or illustrative.

Already decided: see project/2026-11-05-setup-link-plan.md, "The interface". Long steps may only be able to show elapsed time, and the Command Line Tools step shows no estimate, because no reliable figure exists (project/2026-11-05-clean-mac-research.md).

Open, Ben's call: whether Apple's step stays separate, since Homebrew can install those tools itself; which file goes on the Woodcase card (he suggested a real screenshot from `woodcase serve`, and it has to be legible at card size); whether the Jobs card keeps its real task titles. Apply whatever Y6LsGy finds, editing this description if it changes the premise.

Out of scope: pro mode (t5FAqu), which builds on this, and the /remote-control step's content (9WWQm2).

criteria.label: Sleepy stills of every screen in both agent names are reviewed by Ben, recorded in a note
A run with the screens driven by a script reaches done with each state's choices returned to wait as JSON
No card shows invented output, shown by each card's source being listed in a note
On a Mac with no developer tools, the page opens and the agent receives the choices, shown on the clean-Mac run or the VM
With the bootstrap binary unavailable, the same setup finishes in the chat with the same facts, using the raw catalog/tools.json

data.text: Detailed in project/2026-11-05-bootstrap-binary-plan.md and split into child leaves, approved by Ben 2026-11-05. The three criteria moved rather than lapsed: the token refusal and clean-Mac page criteria are on the release and screens leaves, and the chat fallback is on W2yASt, since SETUP.md is what makes it work.

Ben, 2026-11-05: detect also reports what kind of folder this is, because people start in folders that are not projects: home, Desktop, Documents, Downloads, or a generic name like "Claude" or "Claude Code". It only reports; the agent offers to make a project folder and restart there, moving nothing. A Git repo wins over a generic name. Generic names live with the catalog. See project/2026-11-05-bootstrap-binary-plan.md, Decisions.

criteria.label: A table test shows detect reports the folder's kind for home, Desktop, Documents, Downloads, a generic name in any case, an ordinary folder, and a Git repo named Claude, which counts as a project

data.text: Ben, 2026-11-05: step 0 now covers Desktop, Documents, Downloads and generically named folders as well as home; use the folder kind from bootstrap detect, and have the chat fallback make the same check. Where the new folder goes is open: see the binary plan, Still open. Do not move existing files.

criteria.label: Started in Desktop, Documents or a folder named Claude, setup offers a project folder and leaves the starting folder uninitialized

data.text: Ben, 2026-11-05: new project folders default to ~/Projects, with ~/git as the other suggestion. Keep the existing rule: never move what is in the starting folder.
Ben, 2026-11-05: PixelPeeper is MIT. Add the LICENSE as part of this leaf.

Ben, 2026-11-05: the Jobs card keeps its screenshot, because it comes from a public repo. The prototype is the desired design, including the checklist, one-line status, progress fill and tool cards. Woodcase card: pending Ben; comparison of the whole viewer and three real renders at card size says the viewer is illegible at the 440px maximum.

Ben, 2026-11-05: the Mini is available now. How to reach it is still needed from Ben. The first-run VM flow and the Command Line Tools polling need no release; the agent trial needs the public trial release (vHAiCj), which waits until Ben has approved everything that can be approved locally.
Ben, 2026-11-05: publish only after he has approved everything that can be approved locally. A public URL is needed to test the real install path.
Ben, 2026-11-05: Apple's step stays separate, because it could be lengthy. Homebrew will find the tools already there and skip them.

Reach the Mini as agent@sally.local or ben@sally.local (SSH works). Facts are in project/2026-11-05-clean-mac-research.md, "The Mac Mini, as found". agent@ cannot brew install; Tart installs as ben@. 45GB free, so check the VM image size first. It has no display, so someone must use Screen Sharing or VNC to click Apple's Install in the VM.

Ben, 2026-11-05: bottle and release everything. Blocker found: scripts/release refuses a dirty tree, and Jobs, agents and contextfill have uncommitted rule re-renders (Jobs and agents are also one commit ahead). Formula floor is unset; woodcase uses depends_on macos: :sequoia. Release needs the sandbox off. Contextfill has a release.conf with no bottle keys yet; Jobs and agents have no release.conf or formula.

Ben, 2026-11-05: bottle and release everything, and PixelPeeper is MIT. Blocker found: scripts/release refuses a dirty tree. SleepyHollow has uncommitted rule re-renders and one commit ahead; PixelPeeper has an untracked .timetattle-project.json. Neither has a release.conf or formula.

Ben, 2026-11-05: Woodcase card uses three real renders from woodcase-app.pen (Home, Ratings, dark Home) with woodcase shot. Render from a folder with its images/ beside the .pen: Tests/WoodcaseTests/Fixtures has no images, which is why the first render had gray boxes; local/viewer-demo/images has them. The font is right: IBM Plex Sans is cached and no fallback warning was printed.

Graphics check moves to the Mini display (Ben, 2026-11-05), so the Air is not needed. OpenCode credentials: Ben approved copying /Users/ben/git/goodall/.env to the Mini when the trial needs it; do not put it in the repo or the VM, and do not print values. Tart 2.41.1 is at ~agent/tart-install; clone named clean.

Built on branch worktree-agent-aa34ef39cb7b3e35a, not yet integrated. Packages catalog, internal/detect and internal/screen, with internal/cli's read verbs. Samples are in internal/screen/samples and regenerate with go test ./internal/screen -update. Decisions and open problems: project/2026-11-05-bootstrap-seams.md.

Built on branch worktree-agent-aa34ef39cb7b3e35a, not yet integrated. Packages internal/session, internal/server and internal/page (the embed seam), with internal/cli's act verbs. Not run: a real /usr/bin/open and a real browser, since tests use BOOTSTRAP_OPEN=/usr/bin/true and plain HTTP clients. Two open problems for SETUP.md and the trial are in project/2026-11-05-bootstrap-seams.md: nothing tells the agent when to leave a "your turn" screen, and every command writes to ~/.bootstrap, which a sandboxed agent can't reach.

data.text: Ben, 2026-11-05: add a chat screen once the page agent is back: title "Let's talk in {app}.", line "{ai} has a question." No buttons, and it must not show the lost screen, since the agent stops running commands while it waits for a reply in the chat. Open with Ben: whether the CLI gets a free-text message verb; I recommended no, to keep the closed lists.

Released contextfill 0.1.3, job 0.1.0, agents 0.1.0 (arm64_sequoia bottles, Developer ID signed, notarized via keychain profile woodcase-notary, which works for any tool of this team). All pour on this Mac with runtime deps [] (brew info --json=v2: poured_from_bottle true). minos 13.0 for all three; `spctl -a -vv -t install` accepted, source=Notarized Developer ID; `spctl -t exec` rejects any bare CLI ("does not seem to be an app"), woodcase included. job needed a source version: a tarball build printed "job (devel)". agents gained --version. Clean-account pour is still the integrator's VM run.

Squashed to main. Evidence is in the agent's report: 25 states compared at 1440 and 400 wide with scripts/page-compare.sh (MAE 0.0 to 0.1 except explained differences on terminal, apple-ask, the project questions and lost); console empty on all 81 preview states; every request goes to 127.0.0.1 by sleepy wire, though the network was never turned off; lost screen shown live after kill -9. Sleepy flags only the Terminal command line at 400px, which is deliberately clipped with an ellipsis. Not checked: live motion, the eight-bit path, reduced motion, healing after real sleep, browsers other than WebKit. New for Ben to judge: after a click the other choices dim to 45% and the object speeds up. Leaf stays open for Ben's live review (IKa).
